name: Islamic nationalism
summary: Islamic nationalism treats Muslims as a single nation bound by faith rather than by language, ethnicity or territory, and seeks to organise political life around Islamic law and identity. It grew out of anti-colonial Muslim politics (Iqbal, the Muslim League and the Pakistan movement) and later Islamist national movements such as Hamas and Bosnia's Islamic Declaration. It rejects secularism and the separation of religion and state, defends Muslim land against foreign rule, and aims at an Islamic order in which religion shapes law, family, education and culture.
scope: Mainstream religious nationalism among Muslims: the South Asian Muslim nationalism of Iqbal and the Muslim League (two-nation theory, Objectives Resolution), Izetbegovic's Islamic Declaration, and the Hamas Covenant of 1988 as the best-known national-Islamist programme. It excludes the jihadist caliphate project of al-Qaeda and ISIS and secular Arab or Turkish nationalism. Many answers on economic and technical questions are low-confidence inferences, because these texts focus on identity, law and resistance.

keyFigures.name: Muhammad Iqbal
keyFigures.role: Poet-philosopher who proposed a Muslim state in north-west India and rejected separation of religion and state.

keyFigures.name: Muhammad Ali Jinnah
keyFigures.role: Muslim League leader who turned the two-nation theory into the Pakistan movement.

keyFigures.name: Alija Izetbegović
keyFigures.role: Author of the Islamic Declaration and first president of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Islamic sources do not fix an economic system (Islamic Declaration); adherents split between market-friendly and state-directed views.

public-ownership.rationale: No fixed economic system is prescribed; practice varies from state-owned industry in Iran to private enterprise in Pakistan and Turkey.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Izetbegovic's Islamic state would ban alcohol and vice; intoxicants are forbidden in Islamic law, so recreational drug legalization is rejected.

state-harmful.rationale: These movements aim to build an Islamic state (Hamas Art. 9; Islamic Declaration), so the idea that the state is unnecessary is rejected.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Izetbegovic's Islamic state would ban prostitution, and Islamic law forbids extramarital sex.

decide-locally.rationale: Nationalist projects centre on a unified state or ummah rather than devolution; Objectives Resolution does call for a federation, so this is low confidence.

traditional-family.rationale: Hamas Arts. 17-18 describe the Muslim woman as the educator of the next generation and the family as central to Muslim society.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Islamism seeks to order society by Islamic law, which does not recognize same-sex marriage.

more-religion-public.rationale: Making Islam the program of state and society is the core aim: Hamas Art. 1 and 8, Islamic Declaration, and the Objectives Resolution.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Islamic Declaration credits Japan's growth to retained culture and blames secularization for Turkey's stagnation; Hamas Art. 19 wants Islamic art and culture.

gradual-change.rationale: Izetbegovic favoured moral renewal before political change, but Hamas and others favour armed struggle; adherents split.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Hamas Arts. 13 and 32 reject international conferences and initiatives; the UN is seen as dominated by hostile powers.

nation-first.rationale: Iqbal rejected territorial nationalism, but community-first interest (Muslim or ummah) is defended over global cooperation.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Intervention by outside powers is read as imperialism in these movements; Hamas rejects international solutions.

open-borders.rationale: Open borders for Muslims is supported in the ummah ideal, but a general open borders position is not found in the sources.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Islamic Declaration puts moral and religious renewal ahead of technology, but does not oppose technology.

revolution-justified.rationale: Izetbegovic's Declaration envisions a religious-moral revolution followed by political takeover; Hamas treats armed resistance as duty (Art. 12).

experts-over-public.rationale: Izetbegovic favours a trained ideological vanguard, while Objectives Resolution favours elected representatives; no clear stance.

central-planning.rationale: Islamic sources fix no economic system (Islamic Declaration); central planning is not a defining Islamic position.

state-directs-investment.rationale: No economic system is prescribed; practice varies widely.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Islamic law recognizes wages and trade; no Islamic nationalist source calls for abolishing money.

one-party-rule.rationale: Objectives Resolution calls for elected representatives; a single ideological party is not the usual model, though Izetbegovic favoured a vanguard.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Islamism includes both monarchist and republican states; Izetbegovic cited the elected early caliphs as the model.

democracy-best.rationale: Objectives Resolution endorses democracy as defined by Islam, but under divine sovereignty, so "even when voters choose badly" is not accepted without qualification.

workers-councils.rationale: Class-based council rule contradicts Islamic nationalist ideas, which centre on religious community and Islamic law.

right-to-secede.rationale: Muslim nationalism claimed secession from India for Muslim-majority areas, but within Muslim lands the unity ideal opposes breakup; split by whose secession.

political-violence-never.rationale: Hamas Art. 12 and 13 make armed jihad an individual duty and reject political solutions, so political violence is justified.

war-builds-character.rationale: Hamas glorifies jihad and martyrdom as moral discipline; stated mainly for defensive struggle.

separate-church-state.rationale: Iqbal said Europe's greatest blunder was separating church and state; Izetbegovic rejects coexistence of Islamic faith and non-Islamic institutions.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Hamas calls the Koran its constitution (Art. 8) and the Objectives Resolution ties life to the Quran and Sunnah.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The state is the instrument for Islamic order in these movements; privatized courts and defence are alien to them.

military-superiority.rationale: Hamas and Muslim nationalists emphasize armed preparedness and strength against enemies of Muslim land.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Islamic nationalism defines the nation by faith, not ethnicity (Ummah); mixed-ethnic Muslim states are accepted.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Islamism sees history as driven by faith and its decline, not by class conflict.

civilizational-union.rationale: The defining claim: all Muslims form one nation, the Ummah, and should unite (Islamic nationalism article, Iqbal, Izetbegovic's pan-Islamic federation).

self-interest-moral.rationale: Islamic ethics stress duty and mutual responsibility (Hamas Art. 21) over self-interest.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Hamas frames jihad and religious obligation as individual duties above personal preference; community duty is stressed in Islamic ethics.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Izetbegovic praised parts of Western civilization and blamed Turkey's stagnation on secularization, not on industry.

restore-past-order.rationale: Islamism seeks to restore a society ordered by Islamic law, and Rida sought to restore the Caliphate; framed as renewal rather than rejection of progress.

results-over-ideology.rationale: These movements judge policy by fidelity to Islam as the program (Hamas Art. 1), not by pragmatic results.

direct-action.rationale: Hamas favours direct action and jihad, but Pakistan's movement and Izetbegovic worked through parties and education; split.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Wholly outside Islamic nationalist thought, which aims at an Islamic state and society.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Hamas Arts. 17-18 assign distinct roles; abolition is not a goal.

production-for-use.rationale: No economic system is prescribed in Islamic sources.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Islamic law permits trade and profit; the claim comes from Marxism, which these movements reject.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Class dictatorship is a Marxist idea; Islamists reject it.

taxation-theft.rationale: Zakat is a religious obligation, and Islamic states levy taxes; taxation-as-theft is alien.

harm-principle.rationale: Izetbegovic's Islamic state would ban alcohol, prostitution, pornography and gambling, which restricts acts beyond harm to others.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Hamas stresses duties and the Muslim community, and Objectives Resolution grants minority rights by communal faith; rights are not only individual.

state-as-business.rationale: Alien to these movements, which see the state as moral and religious.

media-academia-power.rationale: Hamas Art. 22 claims hostile forces control media and education; adherents view secular elites as hostile.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Islamic nationalism defines the community by faith, and Islam's universalism rejects racial hierarchy.

total-state.rationale: Islam is taken to cover all life (Hamas Art. 1, Islamic Declaration) yet the state is not given total control; split.

national-rebirth.rationale: Izetbegovic calls for religious and moral revolution and renewal; Islamic revival is the shared theme of these movements.

bound-labor.rationale: Serfdom is not part of these movements.

universal-morality.rationale: Islam is held to provide universal truth for all humanity, though knowable through revelation more than reason alone.

single-common-good.rationale: Objectives Resolution ties state to a divinely defined justice and social order rather than competing interests.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Hamas Arts. 11 and 22 reject any Jewish state in Palestine, calling the land Islamic waqf.

revive-national-language.rationale: Islamic nationalism centres on a religious community and Arabic as liturgical language, not on national language revival.

rule-by-example.rationale: Izetbegovic stresses moral example, and the Quranic-model ruler as a pattern (Hamas Art. 8, Prophet as model).

national-self-determination.rationale: Muslim nationalism claimed self-determination for Muslim-majority regions (Iqbal, Muslim League), and Hamas seeks it for Palestinians.

force-without-un.rationale: Hamas rejects international conferences and the UN as a path (Arts. 13, 32), and holds armed resistance legitimate without them.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Islamism takes the revealed law as the guide to society; faith is not subordinate to reason.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Islamic charity (zakat) supports the needy, and the sources set no work requirement; adherents differ on conditioning aid, so the answer is left neutral.

class-collaboration.rationale: Hamas Art. 21 describes Muslim society as mutually responsible, with no class struggle.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Izetbegovic and Hamas Art. 19 value Islamic culture and heritage.

dominated-front.rationale: Pan-Islamic and anti-colonial thought calls for a common front against the West; Hamas Arts. 14 and 23-24 call for unity of Muslim and Arab states.

workers-nation.rationale: The community is defined by faith (Ummah), not class or nation of workers.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Hamas Arts. 17-18 assign women the role of educating the next generation; Islamic law differentiates roles.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The community is united by faith across ethnicities.

state-class-instrument.rationale: A Marxist view; Islamists see the state as a moral and religious institution.

elite-replacement.rationale: Not a theme of Islamic nationalism; a Western-origin conspiracy narrative.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Hamas Arts. 17-18 see women's role as complementary and Islamic, not as systemic disadvantage.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Izetbegovic and Hamas criticize secularized and Western-aligned elites; corruption narrative is common.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Contrary to Islamic ethics on family and life.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The Islamic state enforces moral and religious order (Izetbegovic: bans on alcohol and vice), far beyond a minimal state.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Faith-based community; Islam's universalism does not endorse race hierarchy.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Objectives Resolution promises equality as defined by Islam, but with religious distinctions; equal rights before law are qualified.

socialism-one-country.rationale: A Marxist concept not relevant to these movements.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Hamas Arts. 11 and 22 treat Israel as a foreign invasion of Muslim land.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Muslim nationalism demanded Muslim personal law; the Muslim League opposed a uniform civil framework with Hindus.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: A Hindu demand opposed by Muslim nationalists; cattle slaughter is lawful in Islam.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Hamas Art. 16 wants Islamic education, and Objectives Resolution wants an Islamic ordering of life.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The Objectives Resolution puts authority in God, exercised through the people as a sacred trust; consent matters but is bounded.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Hamas Art. 12 requires armed jihad, and states use force; the principle is rejected.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Islamic ethics stress solidarity and faith in history, not competition.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Adherents oppose bans of Islamist parties but want to bar secular parties in an Islamic state; split.

separated-powers.rationale: Objectives Resolution includes an independent judiciary and fundamental rights; checks are generally accepted.

vanguard-party.rationale: Izetbegovic envisages a small trained ideological vanguard leading Islamic revival.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Hamas Art. 21 describes mutual responsibility and aid to those in need; zakat serves the poor.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Faith-based cohesion is valued, but ethnic diversity within the ummah is accepted; religious diversity is treated as a challenge.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Alien to Islamic constitutional thinking, which favours election or consultation.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Islamic jurists historically debated state price-fixing and the texts here do not choose a side, so adherents are split.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Izetbegovic proposes a pan-Islamic federation transcending national borders; Muslim unity is a core aim.

head-commands-forces.rationale: These texts do not say who commands the army; Islamic nationalist states have run from presidential to parliamentary systems.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Sunni Islam has no bishops; irrelevant structure for these movements.

clerical-rule.rationale: Izetbegovic criticizes ulama as formalistic and Iqbal blamed them for legal immobility; Sunni nationalists do not make scholars rulers.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Hamas Art. 19 demands Islamic art over jahili, and Izetbegovic would ban pornography.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall is not in the texts; Islamic consultation (shura) does not settle early removal by voters.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Hamas condemns alliances like Camp David but pan-Islamic alliance is sought; unstated.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Alien to Islamic law, which permits rent.

people-in-arms.rationale: Hamas Art. 12 makes resistance an individual duty of every Muslim.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The texts do not compare rural and urban life; Islamic tradition values neither above the other.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Pan-Islamic unity and Hamas Art. 14's three circles favour unifying Muslim peoples across borders.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Izetbegovic criticizes the modernist intelligentsia as disconnected from ordinary Muslims, but not educated people generally.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Izetbegovic rejects coexistence of Islam with non-Islamic order; Islam is held to be the true guide.

death-penalty.rationale: Islamic penal law includes capital punishment; Hamas holds enemies of the faith to account; treated as acceptable for terrorism-like gravest crimes by movements in power.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about teaching gender equality, and the statement now asks only about sex education.

reviewHistory.rationale: Hamas Art. 16 wants Islamic-oriented education and distinct roles; gender-equality curricula are opposed.
reviewHistory.author: claude-sonnet-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about teaching gender equality, and the statement now asks only about sex education.
reviewHistory.author: claude-opus-5-5

restrict-pornography.rationale: Izetbegovic's Islamic state would ban pornography.

minority-language-support.rationale: The Objectives Resolution protects minority cultures, but the texts do not mention language schooling or services.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Objectives Resolution lets minorities practice their faiths and develop their cultures.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Moral renewal and conformity to an Islamic order are the aims; eccentricity is not valued.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The Objectives Resolution came from Pakistan's constituent assembly; unresolved for other movements.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Izetbegovic cites the elected early caliphs as a model, not direct popular vote.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Hamas Arts. 11 and 13 forbid ceding any part of Palestine, calling it Islamic waqf, and reject peace initiatives.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Islamic economic thought holds property as a trust under moral limits; the sources do not detail it.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: A Marxist debate that Islamic nationalism does not engage; it rejects Soviet atheism on religious grounds without taking this side.

collective-defense.rationale: Hamas Arts. 14 and 23-24 call on Muslim and Arab states to act together, resembling mutual defence.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Hamas holds Israeli control of Palestine unlawful occupation of Muslim land.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Islamists distrust state control of religion, as in Kemalist secularism, which Izetbegovic criticized.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Muslim nationalists claimed secession themselves; positions diverge for their own states.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Divine sovereignty belongs to God alone (Objectives Resolution); a divine-descent ruler contradicts Islam.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Rulers are bound by divine law (Objectives Resolution: authority is a sacred trust within God's limits).

mixed-constitution.rationale: Classical mixed-constitution theory is not part of Islamic nationalist texts; they stress divine law bounding rulers and people.

leader-cult.rationale: Hamas holds the Prophet as the model (Art. 8); mass praise of a national leader is unlike this.

equal-parenting.rationale: Custody is governed by Islamic family law, which these texts do not spell out; adherents differ on how it applies.

refugee-return.rationale: Hamas insists on the return of Palestinians to the land; Art. 14 makes liberation an individual duty.

women-must-cover.rationale: Islamism orders law by Islamic norms including modest dress; the nationalist texts do not state a legal duty.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Islamic nationalism unites by faith, not language family; Pan-Turkic strands are separate.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Objectives Resolution guarantees minorities faith and culture; Muslims in India sought autonomy for their institutions.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Muslim nationalism rejected remaining a minority in India and demanded a state; it did not tell minorities to fight for equal rights where they live.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Islamists see history as shaped by faith and its decline; materialist explanations are rejected.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Objectives Resolution limits both majority and state by divine law and an independent judiciary; majority power is not unbounded.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Hamas Arts. 17-18 assign women a defined role; parity quotas are not favoured.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Hamas holds armed jihad as the path (Art. 8) and does not wait for conditions.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Islam rejects privilege by birth in principle, but monarchies exist among Islamists; split.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Hamas Art. 16 calls for education in Quran, Sunna and Islamic history.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Islamic nationalism is anti-colonial; tutelage by advanced powers is the colonial claim it opposes.

patriotic-education.rationale: Hamas Art. 15-16 want education that builds Islamic consciousness and loyalty to the cause.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The texts do not debate capitalist crisis theory; Islamic Declaration says Islam fixes no particular economic system.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Islamic order regulates conduct and bans many practices; absolute freedom of association is not the model.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Objectives Resolution guarantees fundamental rights and an independent judiciary.

elective-rulers.rationale: Izetbegovic cites the elected early caliphs as the model; Objectives Resolution requires elected representatives.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Hamas Art. 12 and others legitimize resisting rulers who betray Muslims; Islamists accept resistance to un-Islamic rulers.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Objectives Resolution puts legislative authority under divine limits; parliament is not supreme.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Hamas Art. 21 describes mutual responsibility and aid for those in need.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Islam is a program for politics and society (Hamas Art. 1, Islamic Declaration), so withdrawal is rejected.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Gramscian hegemony is not a framework in these texts; they see rulers as bound by divine law instead.

native-born-offices.rationale: The ummah idea includes converts and Muslim immigrants, but the texts do not address reserving offices for the native-born.

party-own-road.rationale: Izetbegovic and Iqbal want an indigenous Islamic path; not directly stated for parties.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Hamas Art. 11 insists the whole of Palestine be recovered; Pakistan claims Kashmir.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: The comparison of fascism and communism is a Western debate; these texts oppose atheist communism but do not discuss it.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Izetbegovic and Iqbal argue Western secular institutions do not suit Muslims, who need their own Islamic order.

paid-care-work.rationale: Hamas Art. 17 values women's household role but does not call for pay.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Elected representatives are endorsed, but budgets are not mentioned.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Izetbegovic criticizes materialism and Western culture; moral renewal is the aim.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Authority is a sacred trust under divine law, so obedience to the legitimate order is a duty.

non-intervention.rationale: Hamas defends Muslim lands against intervention but supports aid across Muslim states; mixed.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Hamas Arts. 22 and 32 attribute conspiracy to Jews and cite the Protocols; mainstream Muslim nationalism does not; strands split.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Family is the foundation of Muslim society (Hamas Arts. 17-18).

informal-organisation.rationale: Izetbegovic favours a trained vanguard and disciplined movement.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Hamas rejects international conferences, but the order of Islamic law takes precedence over both; split.

religious-nation.rationale: The defining claim: all Muslims form one nation bound by faith (Islamic nationalism; Pakistan as religious nationalism).

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: The ideology is anti-colonial and resists dominant powers.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Objectives Resolution calls for a federation with autonomy, no revenue position.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its value rests on accepting or rejecting common ownership of production, or on private property in general, and the statement now asks only whether personal belongings should stay private where production is held in common.

reviewHistory.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its value rests on accepting or rejecting common ownership of production, or on private property in general, and the statement now asks only whether personal belongings should stay private where production is held in common.
reviewHistory.author: claude-opus-5-5

religion-illusion.rationale: Islamism holds revelation true and the basis of order; religion as illusion is rejected.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: The Marxist view of capitalism's historical role is not engaged; Islamists see Islamic order, not capitalism, as the path of renewal.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Hamas sees women's role in Islamic terms, not an economic transformation.

socialized-care.rationale: Hamas Arts. 17-18 place childcare and household in women's role within the family.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Language purism is not part of Islamic nationalism, which unites by faith; Arabic terms are valued but no purge is called for.

treaties-binding.rationale: Indigenous treaty law is not a topic of these texts; Muslim nationalism did contest colonial treaties but not this form.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Islamists present Islam as a third way between capitalism and communism; Islamic Declaration states Islamic sources fix no system, so medium.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Hamas Art. 11 holds Palestine as Islamic waqf; claims on religious and historical ties are central.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Islamic law treats it as a crime; the nationalist texts do not state it.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Objectives Resolution endorses elected representation and fundamental rights; adherents do not favour suppression as a principle.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Pakistan and Islamists hold blasphemy punishable; Islamism orders society by Islamic law.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Hamas Art. 12 states resistance to enemies of Muslim land is an individual duty of every Muslim.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Qutb-style Islamists accept it, but Iqbal, the Muslim League and Izetbegovic favour reform; strands split.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Hamas Arts. 17-18 and Islamism offer no intersectional analysis.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Islamic law does not recognize gender identity beyond sex.

alienated-labor.rationale: Marxist alienation theory is not engaged by these texts, which frame work in terms of religious duty and moral order.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Adherents deny that Islam is inferior or unfit for society, but they also set Islam against secular Western order, so the statement draws both agreement and rejection.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Objectives Resolution: sovereignty belongs to God alone and the state's authority is a sacred trust.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Islamism opposes bans on religious dress, as in Kemalist Turkey which Izetbegovic criticized.

social-market-economy.rationale: Islamic Declaration says Islam prescribes no particular economic system, so adherents range from market-friendly to statist.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Hamas holds armed defence as an individual duty (Art. 12).

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Pan-Islamic unity favours a Muslim bloc; positions vary.

property-franchise.rationale: Islamic nationalism endorses elected representation and equality, not property qualifications.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Hamas Arts. 17-18 see women's role in Islamic terms; ecofeminist view is alien.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Objectives Resolution requires an independent judiciary and rule under established principles.

racial-franchise.rationale: The community is defined by faith, not race.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Iqbal criticized ulama for legal immobility and sought reconstruction, while Hamas treats the Koran as constitution; strands split.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Islamic law forbids; Islamism orders society by it.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Islamism holds religion central; promoting atheism is opposed.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about prisons or punishment, and the statement now asks only whether the police should be abolished.

reviewHistory.rationale: Izetbegovic's Islamic state enforces law with penalties.

reviewHistory.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about prisons or punishment, and the statement now asks only whether the police should be abolished.
reviewHistory.author: claude-opus-5-5

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Hamas Art. 21 describes community aid and zakat as the social safety net.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Traditional Islamic doctrine restricts, but modernists dissent.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Anti-colonial and anti-Western independence favours removing foreign bases.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Anti-colonial thought stresses economic independence, but the sources do not call for transforming the property system.

filial-duty.rationale: Islamic ethics make lifelong respect for parents a religious duty and Hamas Arts. 17-18 place the family at the centre of Muslim society.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Armed defence of Muslim land is treated as a religious duty (Hamas Covenant on jihad), so killing in defence is not wrong.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Islamist doctrine treats sex and gender roles as fixed by divine creation and law.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Islamist programmes assume a fixed category of women with defined roles in family and law, and so reject this claim.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: The Hamas Covenant makes dying for the sake of Allah its most sublime belief and honours those who fall in the struggle.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Politics is framed as a religious struggle for an Islamic order and against its enemies, though not always as good against evil in the abstract.

culture-before-state.rationale: Iqbal, the Muslim League and Izetbegovic held that Islamic order needs political power and a state, not only cultural renewal.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Scripture and law are held to be divine authority that judges society, not the reverse; the Objectives Resolution places sovereignty in God.

person-over-state.rationale: Objectives Resolution guarantees fundamental rights, but Hamas subordinates the individual to the cause; adherents differ.

spiritual-nature.rationale: The Objectives Resolution places sovereignty with God and Iqbal's and Izetbegovic's writings join faith with politics, rejecting purely material secularism.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Islamic nationalism binds Muslims by faith rather than by race or ethnicity, so racial interest groups are not its basis.

language-defines-nation.rationale: The sources define Islamic nationalism as a nation of believers (the ummah) bound by faith, not by language or ethnicity, so a shared language alone does not make a nation.

communal-electorates.rationale: The Muslim League and the two-nation theory treated Muslims as a separate political community, and separate electorates were a long-standing League demand, though later Islamists stress common Islamic rule.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: The Hamas Covenant describes outside powers working to divide and weaken the Muslim world and Palestine, and the Islamist literature shares a strong anti-Western suspicion.

capital-controls.rationale: Islamic texts set no capital-flow policy, and Islamic-nationalist states differ in practice.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: The Hamas Covenant defends armed resistance as a religious duty, so armed groups outside state forces are legitimate.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: The Hamas Covenant presents fighting for Muslim land as an individual duty of every Muslim, so refusing to fight is not endorsed.

sacred-nation.rationale: Islamic nationalism treats the Muslim nation as a faith community, and the Hamas Covenant makes the homeland a religious trust.

religions-one-truth.rationale: The Hamas Covenant and Islamist sources hold Islam to be the true faith guiding the nation, not one of several paths to the same truth.

ban-fgm.rationale: Adherents split: some Islamic scholars call it un-Islamic, others see it as local custom; the texts do not address it.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Islamic law grants women inheritance and ownership rights but with unequal shares, so a split answer on the statement's 'same right'.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Islamist programmes favour fixed penalties set by sharia, such as hudud, over judicial discretion.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Islamism places life under Quran and Sunnah as the state interprets them, so one interpretation tends to gain official status; adherents differ over how far to tolerate others.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: The Objectives Resolution makes sovereignty divine and elected representatives accountable to it, so elections alone do not make a government legitimate.

premarital-sex.rationale: Hamas Article 17 and Izetbegovic's call for a moral order assign women's role to the family and ban what Islam forbids, so sex outside marriage is condemned.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Hamas Article 17 and Islamism in general treat religion as the foundation of women's dignity and role, so adherents reject the claim that it is a major cause of oppression.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Islamist programmes take the Quran as the divine, binding word, as in the Hamas Covenant and the Islamic Declaration, though Iqbal favoured reconstruction of thought.

national-church-status.rationale: The Objectives Resolution and the Islamic Declaration found the state on Islamic principles, giving Islam a legal standing above other religions.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: The Hamas Covenant calls Palestine an Islamic waqf that may not be ceded and makes defending it a religious duty.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Pan-Islamic solidarity and the Muslim League's two-nation theory frame Muslims abroad as part of one nation owed protection.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: The Objectives Resolution and Islamic Declaration place sovereignty with God and the divine law above man-made legislation, so a rule violating it lacks authority.

missingStatements.text: Religious minorities should be guaranteed freedom to practise their faith and keep their culture, while the state and its laws remain rooted in the majority religion.
missingStatements.rationale: The Objectives Resolution and Izetbegovic both promise minorities religious liberty and protection within a state founded on Islamic principles.
missingStatements.declined: Compound claim that combines minority rights with a religious state, which religious-nation, divine-source-of-authority and religious-exemptions already cover from each side.

notes: Strands differ: Hamas is militant and attaches conspiracy claims to Jews (Arts. 22 and 32), while Iqbal, the Muslim League and Izetbegovic stress moral renewal, elected representation and minority protection. Answers on democracy, jihad and rulers reflect the shared core and mark splits as 0.
